relationships.subject: CGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: each neuropeptide produces TRPM8-dependent cold pain directly

relationships.subject: TLR4
relationships.evidence_quote: Inhibition of CGRP, substance P, or toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) signaling attenuates this phenotype

relationships.subject: TRPM8
relationships.evidence_quote: each induces cold pain that is dependent on the cold-gated channel transient receptor potential melastatin 8 (TRPM8)

relationships.subject: Artemin
relationships.evidence_quote: neurogenic inflammation alters cold sensitivity via localized artemin release that induces cold pain via GFRα3 and TRPM8

key_findings: Lysophosphatidic acid and 4-hydroxy-2-nonenal induce TRPM8-dependent cold pain, attenuated by CGRP, substance P or TLR4 inhibition, with sex differences.
Neuropeptide and mediator-induced cold pain requires artemin and GFRα3 as well as TRPM8.
